verdicts.reason: deposit() dereferences the result of getAccount() at line 7 (account.balance += cents) and line 9 (return account.balance) with no null check, no optional chaining, and no earlier guard. This is the exact pattern of the original transfer() bug: getAccount returns null for a missing or closed account, so a deposit into a closed account throws a TypeError before bus.emit runs. The identical fix applies -- insert `if (!account) throw new Error("account not found or closed");` immediately after the call. It is an exported production function, not test code and not a deliberately unguarded path.
